items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I was hanging aroung Sinton Park again and became aquainted with a boy whose only name I can remember was Harry... Harry was born thief and I started going around stealing things with him

ctx.x: We left this fellow and his wife on the 4th day and Jessie told me that the main reason we left was because he thought that the man was beginning to suspect that his wife was taking a liking to me. Whether that was true, I don't know; but I do know that at that time I did not think about women or girls. I had had some childhood sweethearts but that was nothing serious.

So we came back to Cincinnati and I stayed with Jessie and his uncle for a while. I was hanging aroung Sinton Park again and became aquainted with a boy whose only name I can remember was Harry. He may have been a couple of years older than myself and he had been in and out of reform school many times. Harry was born thief and I started going around stealing things with him and another boy.

Harry was the brain of the gang. He was a very nice looking boy, quite clear and had very nice hair. I never saw him smile or heard him laugh and he seemed to not have any interest in anything except stealing. We would steal silk shirts off the clothes line of people and sell them to pimps in the pool rooms. Cincinnati had plenty of alleys and women hung their washing in the back yards that had gates and were easy to get into.
